images.title: The seconds hand runs 25 seconds from 10
images.purpose: A seconds dial with a ghost hand on 10 and a red hand on 3, the stretch passing 12 shaded, and the working written beside it.
images.composition: A caption at the top, one seconds dial with a ghost start hand, a red stop hand and a shaded stretch between them on the left, and the working written at the right.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. TOP LEFT: the caption The seconds hand runs for 25 seconds in dark #1F2937 sans-serif bold (36 px), left edge at x 100, about y 70. ONE CLOCK, centre at x 400, y 430: a circle 400 px across (spanning x 200 to 600 and y 230 to 630) with a dark teal #0B3C49 rim 14 px thick and a pale face #E8F4F8; 60 small tick marks around the face in dark #2B2B2B, of which 12 are long (4 px wide, from radius 160 to 180 px, at the 12 numbers) and 48 are short (2 px wide, from radius 168 to 180 px); the 12 numbers 1 to 12 in dark #1F2937 sans-serif bold (34 px), centred on a ring of radius 138 px from the centre, 12 at the top, 3 on the right, 6 at the bottom, 9 on the left; a small dark #2B2B2B centre dot 14 px across. The clock has no hour hand and no minute hand, only a seconds dial. WEDGE: a pale vermilion #F7D2C0 wedge (no outline) from the centre out to radius 176 px, from the 300 degree line to the 90 degree line, going clockwise from the start hand to the stop hand (150 degrees wide, 150 degrees is 25 seconds, passing 12), drawn under the hands. START HAND (a pale ghost): a grey #9CA3AF hand 4 px wide and 150 px long, round end, pointing at the number 10 (300 degrees clockwise from 12), its tip at x 270, y 355. STOP HAND: a vermilion #D55E00 seconds hand 5 px wide and 160 px long, round end, pointing at the number 3 (90 degrees clockwise from 12), its tip at x 560, y 430.  RIGHT SIDE, left edge at x 760, in dark bold: three lines at about y 300, y 360 and y 420 (36 px): Start on 10 is 50 seconds, then 50 + 25 = 75, then 75 − 60 = 15 seconds, the number 3. BOTTOM RIGHT, left edge at x 760 and about y 640: The hand stops on 3 (56 px), the largest text in the frame. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: From 10 (50 seconds) 25 seconds more is 75, which is past 60: 75 − 60 = 15 seconds, so the hand stops on 3 after passing 12.
images.description: A seconds dial with a ghost hand on 10 and a red hand on 3, the stretch passing 12 shaded, and the working written beside it.
images.context: Concept image for Drawing the Seconds Hand. It follows the idea of the clock pictures in your maths book (the missing seconds hand drawn after a number of seconds) and shows the concept's own example of 25 seconds from 10.
images.teaching_notes: Let the child count 5 numbers on from 10: 11, 12, 1, 2, 3. The slip to watch: stopping the stretch at 12 and forgetting the seconds that go past it.

image_decisions.why: The dial with the stretch passing 12 shows where the hand stops and why the minute hand moves on.
